prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single universally “best” broker — the right one depends on your budget, health needs, whether you want ACA marketplace plans (with subsidies) or off-exchange/short‑term coverage, and whether you prefer a local in‑person agent or a national online broker. I can help you find the best fit if you tell me your ZIP code, ages, and whether you want marketplace/subsidy eligibility checked.

How to pick the best broker for a self‑employed person in Kansas City, MO
- Use an independent agent/broker (not captive to one carrier). They can shop multiple insurers and compare marketplace vs. off‑exchange options.  
- Confirm the broker is licensed in Missouri (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance or ask the broker for their license number).  
- Prefer brokers who specialize in individual/sole‑proprietor clients and ACA marketplace plans so they know subsidy rules for 1099/self‑employed income.  
- Look for good reviews, transparent fee policy (most agents’ fees are paid by carriers or free to you for ACA plans), and willingness to compare several carriers and explain networks, formularies, and out‑of‑pocket costs.

Good broker options to consider
- Local independent health insurance agencies in the Kansas City area — they’ll help with on‑exchange (Marketplace) enrollment and off‑exchange comparisons and can provide in‑person help (ask for firms that advertise “individual & family plans” and “ACA enrollment”).  
- National online brokers that work well for self‑employed people: HealthSherpa (easy ACA marketplace enrollment and subsidy estimates), eHealth (broad carrier comparisons), and GoHealth. These are useful if you prefer an online experience and quotes quickly.  
- A broker who is a NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) member or certified ACA assister can be an added plus.

Questions to ask any broker/agent
- Are you licensed in Missouri? What’s your license number?  
- Do you specialize in individual/marketplace plans and self‑employed clients?  
- Do you charge any fees to me? (Most don’t for Marketplace plans.)  
- Which carriers/plans will you compare? Will you include both on‑exchange and off‑exchange options?  
- Can you estimate my subsidy/premium tax credit based on my expected 1099 income?  
- How will you help if I need to file an appeal or have a claims issue?  
- Can you explain network rules, primary care/referral requirements, and prescription coverage for the plans you recommend?

What to have ready when you talk to a broker
- ZIP code, household size, ages of everyone to be insured, estimated 2026 household income (including 1099/self‑employed income), and any regular prescription meds or preferred doctors/hospitals.

Other tips specific to the self‑employed
- Make sure the broker can handle subsidy estimates and advise about how changing your reported income affects premium tax credits.  
- If you’re eligible for an HSA‑qualified high‑deductible plan and want tax advantages, ask about HSA compatibility.  
- If you expect variable income, discuss safe ways to estimate income for marketplace subsidy reconciliation to avoid large surprises at tax time.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist well‑rated local Kansas City brokers/agencies if you give your ZIP code (I can’t browse from here, but I can suggest how to search and what to look for), or  
- Walk through a quick estimate to see whether you’re likely to qualify for Marketplace subsidies if you tell me household size, ages and expected 2026 income.

Which would you like to do?
